  "content": "---\nname: ruff-release-readiness-sweep\ndescription: |\n  Systematic lint triage workflow to prepare a Python codebase for release.\n  Use when: (1) user asks to \"clean up codebase for release\", (2) pre-release\n  quality sweep needed, (3) reducing lint errors from hundreds to style-only.\n  Prioritizes real bugs (F821, syntax) over style issues (E501, N806) and uses\n  ruff auto-fix to eliminate safe violations without manual edits.\nauthor: Claude Code\nversion: 1.0.0\n---\n\n# Ruff Release Readiness Sweep\n\n## Problem\n\nA codebase has accumulated hundreds of lint violations. Not all are equal —\nsome are real runtime bugs (undefined names, syntax errors), others are style\npreferences (line length, naming). Fixing them in the wrong order wastes time.\n\n## Priority Order (Fix in This Sequence)\n\n| Priority | Rule(s) | Why | Action |\n|----------|---------|-----|--------|\n| 1 | Syntax errors (E9xx) | File can't even be parsed | Fix manually |\n| 2 | F821 (undefined-name) | Real runtime `NameError` bugs | Fix manually |\n| 3 | F811 (redefined-while-unused) | Duplicate definitions / dead code | Fix manually |\n| 4 | E741 (ambiguous-variable-name) | `l` vs `1` confusion | Rename manually |\n| 5 | F401 (unused-import) | Dead imports | `ruff check --fix` |\n| 6 | W29x (whitespace) | Trailing/mixed whitespace | `ruff check --fix` |\n| 7 | F841 (unused-variable) | Minor: assigned but never read | Optional |\n| 8 | E501 (line-too-long) | Style only | Optional / skip |\n| 9 | N806/N812/N814 (naming) | Often intentional (math vars) | Optional / skip |\n\n## Workflow\n\n```bash\n# Step 1: Get full picture (save output for tracking)\nruff check src/ 2>&1 | tee /tmp/lint_before.txt\ngrep -c \"error\" /tmp/lint_before.txt  # total count\n\n# Step 2: Identify critical violations\nruff check src/ | grep -E \"^.*\\s(E9|F821|F811|E741)\" | head -50\n\n# Step 3: Fix critical violations manually (see patterns below)\n\n# Step 4: Apply safe auto-fixes\nruff check src/ --fix --select F401,W291,W293,W292,F541,E711,E712\n\n# Step 5: Verify improvement\nruff check src/ 2>&1 | tee /tmp/lint_after.txt\ngrep -c \"error\" /tmp/lint_after.txt\n\n# Step 6: Confirm tests still pass\nuv run pytest tests/ -q\n```\n\n## Common F821 Patterns (Undefined Name)\n\n### Comprehension variable typo\n```python\n# WRONG: unpacks as (_, _, ts) but uses t\nrecent = [t for _, _, ts in self.history if time.time() - ts < 3600]\n\n# CORRECT: use the actual unpacking variable\nrecent = [ts for _, _, ts in self.history if time.time() - ts < 3600]\n```\n\n### Missing import for used name\n```python\n# WRONG: asyncio used but not imported\nasync def restart():\n    await asyncio.sleep(1)  # NameError at runtime\n\n# CORRECT: add the import\nimport asyncio\n```\n\n### TYPE_CHECKING guard for forward references\n```python\n# WRONG: circular import\nfrom cohezion.compound.thermodynamic_metrics import ThermodynamicState\n\n# CORRECT: type-only import (no runtime cost)\nfrom typing import TYPE_CHECKING\nif TYPE_CHECKING:\n    from cohezion.compound.thermodynamic_metrics import ThermodynamicState\n```\n\n### Dead code after unconditional raise (F821 false positive)\nCode after `raise SomeException(...)` can never execute, but ruff still\nvalidates it. Options: delete the dead code, or restructure to avoid.\n\n## Common F811 Patterns (Redefined While Unused)\n\n### Duplicate class methods (second definition wins, first is dead)\n```python\nclass MyClass:\n    def get_truth_anchors(self): ...  # DEAD — defined again below\n    def remember_fact(self): ...      # DEAD\n    # ... 300 lines of other methods ...\n    def get_truth_anchors(self): ...  # LIVE — this is the one that runs\n    def remember_fact(self): ...      # LIVE\n```\nFix: delete the earlier (dead) definitions.\n\n### Import shadowed by local class definition\n```python\nfrom module import CompoundCycleResult, CompoundCycleReport  # imported\n# ... later in same file ...\nclass CompoundCycleResult: ...   # shadows the import — F811\nclass CompoundCycleReport: ...   # shadows the import — F811\n```\nFix: remove the shadowed imports from the `from ... import` statement.\n\n## Common E741 Patterns (Ambiguous Variable Name)\n\n```python\n# WRONG: l looks like 1\nlines = [l for l in content.splitlines()]\nlv = tuple(int(x) for x in latest.split(\".\"))\n\n# CORRECT: rename to descriptive alternatives\nlines = [ln for ln in content.splitlines()]   # ln for \"line\"\nlv = tuple(int(x) for x in latest.split(\".\")) # lv for \"latest version\"\n```\n\n## Gamma Release Decision Criteria\n\nAfter sweep, categorize remaining violations:\n- **Block release**: Any F821, syntax errors, F811 with active duplicates\n- **Acceptable for gamma**: F841 (unused vars), E501 (line length), N806 (naming)\n- **Post-gamma cleanup**: Files over 500-line limit, large-scale refactors\n\nA codebase is gamma-ready when ALL critical violations are zero,\neven if style violations remain.\n\n## Verification\n\n```bash\n# Confirm zero critical violations\nruff check src/ | grep -cE \"F821|F811|E741|E9[0-9]{2}\" || echo \"0 critical\"\n\n# Confirm test suite intact\nuv run pytest tests/ -q --tb=no | tail -3\n```\n"
}

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The TC001 rule ("move import into `TYPE_CHECKING` block") is dangerous when applied blindly. It moves imports that are **only used in type annotations** into `TYPE_CHECKING`, which means they're only available during static analysis. But if tests or runtime code needs to `patch("module.ClassName")`, the name won't exist at runtime. This is the classic TC001 trap — it optimizes import speed but breaks runtime patching.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The `learning/__init__.py` uses `from __future__ import annotations` (line 8), which makes all annotations strings. So `TemplateEngine` on lines 85 and 88 is used as a string annotation — it's never evaluated at runtime. But ruff sees it as undefined. This needs a `TYPE_CHECKING` import. Since this file uses `from __future__ import annotations`, the TYPE_CHECKING import is actually the correct pattern here.

     1→# Serena MCP Plugin — Investigation & Recommendation
     2→
     3→## Context
     4→
     5→Serena is a Claude Code plugin (by Oraios) that provides semantic code analysis via Language Server Protocol (LSP). It's installed as a Claude Code plugin at `~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/serena/`. It launches via `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena serena start-mcp-server`.
     6→
     7→**Problem**: Serena crashes on startup every session with:
     8→```
     9→SerenaConfigError: `projects` key not found in Serena configuration.
    10→Please update your `serena_config.yml` file.
    11→```
    12→This causes a 30-second connection timeout on every Claude Code session start.
    13→
    14→## Root Cause
    15→
    16→The config at `~/.serena/serena_config.yml` is missing a required `projects` key. Serena's `SerenaConfig.from_config_file()` (line 751) raises `SerenaConfigError` if this key is absent. The config was likely created before Serena added this requirement.
    17→
    18→**Current config** (`~/.serena/serena_config.yml`):
    19→```yaml
    20→language_backend: LSP
    21→web_dashboard: true
    22→web_dashboard_open_on_launch: false
    23→# ... other settings, but NO projects key
    24→```
    25→
    26→**Fix** (if we want to keep Serena): Add a `projects` key pointing to the cohezion repo:
    27→```yaml
    28→projects:
    29→  - /home/mike-anderson/dev/cohezion
    30→```
    31→
    32→## Recommendation: Remove Serena
    33→
    34→**Serena is redundant.** Every capability it provides is already covered by existing tools, often better:
    35→
    36→| Serena Capability | Already Covered By | Quality |
    37→|---|---|---|
    38→| Code navigation (go to definition, find references) | Built-in `LSP` tool in Claude Code | Equal or better |
    39→| Semantic code search | `vexor search` (semantic) + `Grep`/`Glob` (exact) | Better (vexor has project-aware indexing) |
    40→| Codebase understanding | Built-in `Read`, Explore agent, vexor | Better (native context) |
    41→| Refactoring suggestions | Claude Code itself (direct code editing) | Better |
    42→| Symbol lookup | Built-in `LSP` tool | Equal |
    43→
    44→**Costs of keeping Serena:**
    45→- 30-second timeout penalty on every session start (even when fixed, LSP init adds latency)
    46→- Another LSP server running alongside Claude Code's built-in one (resource waste)
    47→- Config maintenance burden (projects list must be updated per-repo)
    48→- Plugin update risk (config format already broke once)
    49→
    50→**The fix is trivial, but the value is near-zero.** Claude Code's built-in LSP + vexor + Grep already provide superior code intelligence with zero config.
    51→

#### **2. LEGACY COMPATIBILITY WRAPPER OVERHEAD [MEDIUM-HIGH IMPACT]**
- **Problem:** `compat.py` preserves 15-parameter interface for `CompoundExecutor` to maintain backward compatibility with old API
  - Old: `CompoundExecutor.__init__()` accepts 16 different optional parameters
  - New: `core/executor.py` has clean 4-5 parameter design
  - Gap: `compat.py` bridges them but adds confusion
- **Impact:** Callers must decide whether to use `cohezion.compound.CompoundExecutor` (legacy) vs `cohezion.compound.core.executor.CompoundExecutor` (new)
- **Observation:** Only **2 files** in the codebase import from `cohezion.compound.executor` (old API):

  - `src/cohezion/protocols/a2a_server.py`
- **Recommendation:** Migrate these 2 files to new API, then delete `compat.py` and old `executor.py`. Force all callers to use `core.executor.CompoundExecutor`.

#### **3. DUPLICATE METRICS MODULES [MEDIUM-HIGH IMPACT - 350+ LOC]**
- **Problem:** Metrics scattered across 5 modules:
  - `metrics.py` (old, 135 lines)
  - `analytics/metrics.py` (new, 163 lines)
  - `global_metrics_aggregator.py` (640 lines) - overlaps with both
  - `thermodynamic_metrics.py` (565 lines) - thermal-specific metrics
  - `model_quality_classifier.py` (527 lines) - quality metrics
- **Root Cause:** Incremental refactoring left old files unreferenced
- **Impact:**

  - 3 different ways to record execution metrics
- **Recommendation:** Consolidate to single `analytics/metrics.py`. Thermal and quality metrics become **sub-analyzers** (composition over separate modules).

#### **4. GOD OBJECT: ExecutionAlignmentAnalyzer [MEDIUM-HIGH IMPACT]**
- **Problem:** `request_alignment_analyzer.py` is 960 lines with 20+ methods in 1 class:
  - `analyze()` - main entry point
  - `_validate_constraints()`, `_check_completeness()`, `_check_drift_risk()`
  - `_estimate_tokens()`, `_estimate_cost()`, `_estimate_execution_time()`
  - `_assess_model_capability()`, `_assess_skill_coherence()`
  - `_predict_failure_probability()`, `_analyze_safety_concerns()`
  - Plus 10+ more responsibilities
- **Impact:** Single change (e.g., cost estimation logic) requires touching 960-line file. Hard to test/reuse individual concerns.
- **Recommendation:** Break into 6 focused classes:
  - `ConstraintValidator` (validates inputs)
  - `TokenCostEstimator` (estimates tokens/cost)
  - `CapabilityAssessor` (checks model suitability)
  - `DriftRiskAnalyzer` (coherence drift prediction)
  - `SafetyAnalyzer` (guardrail concerns)
  - `RequestAlignmentAnalyzer` (orchestrates above)

#### **5. MASSIVE EXECUTOR CLASS [MEDIUM IMPACT]**

  - Inflection point logging (lines 760-850)
  - Factory pattern (lines 900-1050)

- **Observation:** New `core/executor.py` (206 lines) is the correct pattern. Old `executor.py` should be deleted after migration.

     1→"""Elegant simplified compound executor.
     2→
     3→Replaces the 1,106-line monster with a clean, focused implementation.
     4→Single responsibility: execute tasks with optional analysis.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from __future__ import annotations
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import time
    11→from dataclasses import dataclass
    12→from typing import Any, Callable
    13→
    14→from cohezion.compound.models import (
    15→    AnalysisReport,
    16→    ExecutionContext,
    17→    ExecutionMetrics,
    18→    ExecutionResult,
    19→    Task,
    20→)
    21→
    22→
    23→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    24→
    25→
    26→@dataclass
    27→class ExecutionConfig:
    28→    """Configuration for execution."""
    29→
    30→    max_retries: int = 3
    31→    retry_delay_seconds: float = 1.0
    32→    enable_analysis: bool = True
    33→    enable_checkpointing: bool = True
    34→
    35→
    36→class CompoundExecutor:
    37→    """Clean, focused executor.
    38→
    39→    Single responsibility: execute tasks with optional analysis.
    40→    No god object - accepts analyzers and persisters as plugins.
    41→    """
    42→
    43→    def __init__(
    44→        self,
    45→        execute_fn: Callable[[Task, dict[str, Any]], tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]],
    46→        config: ExecutionConfig | None = None,
    47→        analyzer: Callable[[ExecutionResult, Task], AnalysisReport] | None = None,
    48→        persister: Callable[[ExecutionContext, ExecutionResult], None] | None = None,
    49→    ):
    50→        """Initialize with minimal dependencies.
    51→
    52→        Args:
    53→            execute_fn: Core execution logic (task, context) -> (output, metrics)
    54→            config: Execution configuration
    55→            analyzer: Optional post-execution analysis
    56→            persister: Optional vault persistence
    57→        """
    58→        self.execute_fn = execute_fn
    59→        self.config = config or ExecutionConfig()
    60→        self.analyzer = analyzer
    61→        self.persister = persister
    62→
    63→    def execute(
    64→        self,
    65→        task: Task,
    66→        context: ExecutionContext | None = None,
    67→    ) -> ExecutionResult:
    68→        """Execute task with retry logic.
    69→
    70→        Clean implementation vs the 1,106-line monster.
    71→        """
    72→        if context is None:
    73→            context = ExecutionContext(
    74→                session_id=f"session-{id(task)}",
    75→                task=task,
    76→            )
    77→
    78→        # Attempt execution with retries
    79→        for attempt in range(self.config.max_retries + 1):
    80→            context.attempt_number = attempt
    81→
    82→            result = self._attempt_execution(task, context)
    83→
    84→            if result.success:
    85→                return self._finalize_success(result, context)
    86→
    87→            if attempt == self.config.max_retries:
    88→                return self._finalize_failure(result, context)
    89→
    90→            # Retry logic
    91→            logger.warning(f"Attempt {attempt + 1} failed, retrying...")
    92→            time.sleep(self.config.retry_delay_seconds)
    93→            context = context.with_retry()
    94→
    95→        # Should never reach here
    96→        return result
    97→
    98→    def _attempt_execution(
    99→        self,
   100→        task: Task,
   101→        context: ExecutionContext,
   102→    ) -> ExecutionResult:
   103→        """Single execution attempt."""
   104→        start_time = time.time()
   105→
   106→        try:
   107→            # Execute user-provided function
   108→            output, metrics_dict = self.execute_fn(task, context)
   109→
   110→            duration = time.time() - start_time
   111→
   112→            return ExecutionResult(
   113→                success=True,
   114→                output=output,
   115→                metrics=ExecutionMetrics(
   116→                    duration_seconds=duration,
   117→                    **metrics_dict,
   118→                ),
   119→            )
   120→
   121→        except Exception as e:
   122→            duration = time.time() - start_time
   123→
   124→            return ExecutionResult(
   125→                success=False,
   126→                output=str(e),
   127→                metrics=ExecutionMetrics(duration_seconds=duration),
   128→                error_type=type(e).__name__,
   129→                error_message=str(e),
   130→            )
   131→
   132→    def _finalize_success(
   133→        self,
   134→        result: ExecutionResult,
   135→        context: ExecutionContext,
   136→    ) -> ExecutionResult:
   137→        """Finalize successful execution."""
   138→        # Run analysis if configured
   139→        if self.config.enable_analysis and self.analyzer:
   140→            report = self.analyzer(result, context.task)
   141→
   142→            if report.retry_recommended and context.attempt_number < self.config.max_retries:
   143→                # Trigger retry via exception (simplified flow)
   144→                logger.info("Analysis recommends retry")
   145→                return self._trigger_retry(result, context)
   146→
   147→        # Persist if configured
   148→        if self.config.enable_checkpointing and self.persister:
   149→            self.persister(context, result)
   150→
   151→        return result
   152→
   153→    def _finalize_failure(
   154→        self,
   155→        result: ExecutionResult,
   156→        context: ExecutionContext,
   157→    ) -> ExecutionResult:
   158→        """Finalize failed execution after all retries."""
   159→        logger.error(f"Task failed after {self.config.max_retries + 1} attempts")
   160→
   161→        # Persist failure for analysis
   162→        if self.config.enable_checkpointing and self.persister:
   163→            self.persister(context, result)
   164→
   165→        return result
   166→
   167→    def _trigger_retry(
   168→        self,
   169→        last_result: ExecutionResult,
   170→        context: ExecutionContext,
   171→    ) -> ExecutionResult:
   172→        """Trigger a retry with modified context."""
   173→        # Simplified: just try again
   174→        logger.info("Retrying with analysis guidance")
   175→        return self.execute(context.task, context.with_retry())
   176→
   177→
   178→# Convenience function for simple executions
   179→def execute_simple(
   180→    task_description: str,
   181→    execute_fn: Callable[[], str],
   182→) -> ExecutionResult:
   183→    """Execute simple task without complex setup.
   184→
   185→    For one-off executions without retry or analysis.
   186→    """
   187→    start_time = time.time()
   188→

# Compound Engineering Module Simplification — Implementation Plan

## Overview

Three phases of surgical cleanup: delete duplicates, split the API monolith, and clean up compound exports. Each phase is independently verifiable and shippable.

---

## Phase A: Delete Dead Weight

**Goal:** Remove two duplicate modules and fix any imports referencing them.

**Risk Level:** LOW — These are duplicates with canonical versions already in place.

### Step A.1: Identify all imports of the duplicate files

Before deleting, confirm which files import from the duplicates. The information provided says these are duplicates, but we need to verify no code path exclusively depends on the duplicate versions.

**Commands (read-only verification):**
```bash
rg "from cohezion.compound.exp_persistence.vault" src/ tests/ --files-with-matches
rg "from cohezion.compound.exp_persistence import" src/ tests/ --files-with-matches
rg "from cohezion.compound.metrics" src/ tests/ --files-with-matches
rg "import cohezion.compound.metrics" src/ tests/ --files-with-matches
```

### Step A.2: Delete `src/cohezion/compound/exp_persistence/vault.py`

- **Delete:** `src/cohezion/compound/exp_persistence/vault.py`
- **Possibly delete:** `src/cohezion/compound/exp_persistence/__init__.py` if the directory becomes empty (check for other files first)
- **Possibly delete:** the `exp_persistence/` directory itself if empty
- **Modify:** Any file identified in A.1 that imports from `cohezion.compound.exp_persistence.vault` — change to `cohezion.persistence.vault` (the canonical location)
- **Modify:** `src/cohezion/compound/__init__.py` — remove any re-export of `exp_persistence.vault` symbols

### Step A.3: Delete `src/cohezion/compound/metrics.py`

- **Delete:** `src/cohezion/compound/metrics.py`
- **Modify:** Any file identified in A.1 that imports from `cohezion.compound.metrics` — change to `cohezion.analytics.metrics` (the canonical location)
- **Modify:** `src/cohezion/compound/__init__.py` — remove any re-export of root `metrics` symbols that pointed to the duplicate

### Step A.4: Verify Phase A

```bash
uv run pytest tests/ -q                    # All 4,100+ tests pass
rg "compound.exp_persistence" src/ tests/   # Zero hits
rg "compound.metrics" src/ tests/           # Only hits should be analytics/metrics or similar canonical paths
uv run python -c "from cohezion.compound import *"  # No import errors
```

**Deliverable:** Two fewer files, zero duplicate code paths, all tests green.

---

## Phase B: Split API Monolith

**Goal:** Break `api/__init__.py` (1,535 lines) into focused route modules under `api/routes/`, with shared schemas extracted.

**Risk Level:** MEDIUM — Many endpoints, must preserve exact behavior. The seams are clear but the wiring must be precise.

### Step B.0: Analyze the current API structure

Before splitting, catalog the current `api/__init__.py` to understand:
- Which endpoints exist (all 55+)
- Which share state (app-level singletons like `_vae_trainer`, `_rl_policy`)
- Which Pydantic models are defined inline
- What middleware/startup/shutdown hooks exist

This determines the split boundaries. Based on the requirements, the split is:

| Module | Endpoints | Shared State |
|--------|-----------|--------------|
| `health.py` | `/health`, `/status`, `/version`, readiness probes | None |
| `flume.py` | FLUME VAE training, sampling, checkpoint endpoints | `_vae_trainer` singleton |
| `rl.py` | RL training, policy, reward endpoints | `_rl_policy` singleton |
| `compound.py` | Compound execution, skill refinement, journey tracking | `get_executor()` |
| `metrics.py` | Metrics, observability, dashboard data | `GlobalMetricsAggregator` |

### Step B.1: Create `src/cohezion/api/schemas.py`

- **Create:** `src/cohezion/api/schemas.py`
- **Content:** Extract ALL Pydantic request/response models currently defined inline in `api/__init__.py`
- **Target size:** Under 300 lines. If it exceeds this, split into `schemas/compound.py`, `schemas/flume.py`, etc.
- **Rule:** Only data models (BaseModel subclasses), no route logic, no app state

### Step B.2: Create `src/cohezion/api/state.py`

- **Create:** `src/cohezion/api/state.py`
- **Content:** App-level singletons and their accessor functions:
  - `_vae_trainer` and `get_vae_trainer()` / `reset_flume_vae()`
  - `_rl_policy` and `get_rl_policy()` / `reset_rl_policy()`
  - `get_executor()` (if it lives in API layer, not compound layer)
  - Any other module-level state shared across routes
- **Why:** Routes import state from one place. Prevents circular imports. Enables test fixtures to reset state cleanly.

### Step B.3: Create route modules

Create `src/cohezion/api/routes/__init__.py` (empty or with router aggregation).

**Create each route module following this pattern:**

```python
# src/cohezion/api/routes/health.py
from fastapi import APIRouter

router = APIRouter(tags=["health"])

@router.get("/health")
async def health():
    ...
```

Files to create:
- `src/cohezion/api/routes/__init__.py`
- `src/cohezion/api/routes/health.py` — health, status, version, readiness
- `src/cohezion/api/routes/flume.py` — FLUME VAE endpoints, imports `_vae_trainer` from `state.py`
- `src/cohezion/api/routes/rl.py` — RL endpoints, imports `_rl_policy` from `state.py`
- `src/cohezion/api/routes/compound.py` — compound execution endpoints
- `src/cohezion/api/routes/metrics.py` — metrics/observability endpoints

**Each route file:**
- Defines an `APIRouter` with appropriate tags and prefix
- Imports schemas from `api/schemas.py`
- Imports shared state from `api/state.py`
- Stays under 300 lines

### Step B.4: Rewrite `src/cohezion/api/__init__.py`

- **Modify:** `src/cohezion/api/__init__.py`
- **New content (~50-80 lines):**
  - FastAPI app creation
  - Middleware registration (CORS, etc.)
  - `app.include_router(...)` for each route module
  - Startup/shutdown event handlers
  - Re-export `reset_flume_vae`, `reset_rl_policy` for test compatibility (these are referenced by `tests/conftest.py`)
- **Critical:** `from cohezion.api import reset_flume_vae` must still work (tests depend on it)

### Step B.5: Update test imports

- **Modify:** `tests/conftest.py` — verify `cohezion.api._vae_trainer = None` still works (now via `cohezion.api.state._vae_trainer`)
- **Option A:** Keep re-exports in `api/__init__.py` so `cohezion.api._vae_trainer` still resolves
- **Option B:** Update `conftest.py` to use `cohezion.api.state._vae_trainer = None`
- **Recommendation:** Option A for backward compatibility, with a comment noting the canonical location

### Step B.6: Verify Phase B

```bash
uv run pytest tests/ -q                           # All tests pass
uv run python -c "from cohezion.api import app; print(len(app.routes))"  # Same endpoint count as before
wc -l src/cohezion/api/__init__.py                 # Under 100 lines
wc -l src/cohezion/api/routes/*.py                 # Each under 300 lines
wc -l src/cohezion/api/schemas.py                  # Under 300 lines
rg "from cohezion.api import" tests/ --files-with-matches  # All still resolve
```

**Deliverable:** API monolith replaced by 7-8 focused files, identical endpoint behavior, all tests green.

---

## Phase C: Clean Compound Exports

**Goal:** Simplify `compound/__init__.py` from 55+ symbols with confusing aliases down to a clean public API.

**Risk Level:** MEDIUM-HIGH — External callers depend on specific import paths. Must migrate callers before changing exports.

### Step C.1: Catalog current exports and their consumers

Categorize the 55+ symbols in `compound/__init__.py` into:

| Category | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Used externally (by files outside `compound/`) | Keep in public API |
| Used only internally (within `compound/`) | Remove from `__init__.py`, use direct imports |
| Aliases with confusing dual naming | Collapse to single canonical name |
| Dead exports (imported by nobody) | Remove |

**Key external consumers to trace:**
```bash
rg "from cohezion.compound import" src/ --files-with-matches | rg -v "compound/"
```

### Step C.2: Resolve the CompoundExecutor naming

Current confusion:
- `CompoundExecutor` — aliased from `compat.py` (legacy wrapper)
- `NewCompoundExecutor` — from `core/executor.py` (clean implementation)

**Resolution:**
- `CompoundExecutor` becomes the canonical name, pointing to `core/executor.py`
- `NewCompoundExecutor` is removed as an export
- `LegacyCompoundExecutor` (optional) — alias for the old `executor.py` class during migration

### Step C.3: Migrate external callers of legacy executor

Each caller needs individual attention:

| File | Current Import | Migration |
|------|---------------|-----------|
| `api/__init__.py` (now `api/routes/compound.py`) | `get_executor` from legacy | Update to use new executor's factory |
| `a2a_server.py` | `CompoundExecutor` from compat | Will automatically get new executor after C.2 |
| `ucp_capability_handler.py` | `CompoundExecutor` from compat | Same as above |
| `swarm/team_execution.py` | `get_executor` from legacy | Update factory function |

**For each caller:**
1. Check which methods/attributes of the executor they use
2. Verify the new executor supports those methods (or add adapters)
3. Update the import
4. Run that file's tests specifically

### Step C.4: Rewrite `compound/__init__.py`

- **Modify:** `src/cohezion/compound/__init__.py`
- **New content (~30-50 lines):**
  - Import and export only the essential public API
  - Single `CompoundExecutor` pointing to `core/executor.py`
  - `ExecutionResult` from its canonical location
  - Key components: `SkillRefiner`, `RetrospectionEngine`, `JourneyTracker`, etc.
  - `__all__` list explicitly declaring the public surface
- **Remove:** All dual aliases, internal-only symbols, dead exports

### Step C.5: Evaluate legacy executor deletion

After all callers are migrated (Step C.3):
- If no remaining imports of `compound/executor.py` exist → delete it
- If some callers still need migration → keep with a deprecation comment and track as follow-up
- Run: `rg "from cohezion.compound.executor import\|from cohezion.compound import.*Executor" src/ tests/`

**Decision point:** If the legacy executor has unique logic not in the new executor (the 11-step pipeline), that logic needs to be ported to plugins for the new executor before deletion. This may be out of scope for this plan — flag it if so.

### Step C.6: Delete compat.py (if safe)

- After C.2 makes `CompoundExecutor` point to `core/executor.py`, `compat.py` should have zero consumers
- **Verify:** `rg "from cohezion.compound.compat import\|from cohezion.compound import.*compat" src/ tests/`
- If zero hits → **Delete:** `src/cohezion/compound/compat.py`

### Step C.7: Verify Phase C

```bash
uv run pytest tests/ -q                            # All tests pass
uv run python -c "from cohezion.compound import CompoundExecutor; print(CompoundExecutor.__module__)"
# Should print: cohezion.compound.core.executor

uv run python -c "from cohezion.compound import __all__; print(len(__all__))"
# Should be ~15-20, not 55+

rg "NewCompoundExecutor" src/ tests/               # Zero hits
rg "from cohezion.compound.compat" src/ tests/     # Zero hits (if compat deleted)
```

**Deliverable:** Clean `__init__.py` with explicit `__all__`, single canonical `CompoundExecutor`, compat layer removed.

---

## Sequencing and Dependencies

```
Phase A (delete duplicates)     ← Independent, do first (lowest risk, builds confidence)
    ↓
Phase B (split API monolith)    ← Independent of A, but do second (medium risk)
    ↓
Phase C (clean compound exports) ← Depends on Phase B completing (compound.py route needs to exist before changing executor imports in API)
```

Phase A and Phase B could technically run in parallel, but sequential execution is safer — each phase's test run validates the codebase before the next phase modifies it.

## Risk Summary

| Phase | Risk | Mitigation |
|-------|------|------------|
| A | LOW — Deleting known duplicates | Verify zero unique consumers before deletion |
| B | MEDIUM — Many endpoints to wire correctly | Split one route group at a time, test after each |
| C | MEDIUM-HIGH — External callers + naming changes | Migrate callers individually, verify each caller's tests |

## Estimated Scope

| Phase | Files Created | Files Modified | Files Deleted | Lines Changed (est.) |
|-------|--------------|----------------|---------------|---------------------|
| A | 0 | 2-5 | 2-3 | ~50 |
| B | 7-8 | 3-5 | 0 | ~1,600 (moved, not new) |
| C | 0 | 6-10 | 1-2 | ~200 |

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The plan follows the **compound engineering principle** itself: "every feature makes future features easier." By cleaning exports first (Phase 1), we establish the canonical API surface. Then splitting the API monolith (Phase 2) becomes cleaner because the compound imports in the new route modules use the simplified API from Phase 1. The phases compound on each other.

The key architectural insight: `compound/__init__.py` currently imports from `compat.py` which imports from `executor.py` which imports from `models.py` — a 4-hop chain. After Phase 1, external code imports directly from the clean source: `__init__.py` → `core/executor.py` + `models.py`. Two hops, zero wrappers.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
